turns.speaker: Steve
turns.text:
Absolutely! Let's think about a scenario in psychology known as the Zeigarnik Effect. This phenomenon suggests that people often remember uncompleted or interrupted tasks more vividly than completed ones.

In our case, John is driving and speaking with his spouse, Carol, about something personal. Suddenly, someone calls out his name. John, being startled and focused on the interruption, might forget what he was initially discussing with Carol. Now, to fill the gap in the conversation and address the interruption, John may unwittingly reveal a secret he had intended to keep from Carol.

This situation highlights how interruptions can lead to memory lapses and, in some cases, inadvertently disclose sensitive information. It's a great example of how our cognitive processes and emotional responses can interact in complex and sometimes unexpected ways.
